poam_items.finding:
Multifactor authentication (MFA) has not been fully deployed across all user accounts with access to systems processing CUI. Approximately 40% of end-user accounts and all privileged accounts are enrolled in Azure AD MFA. Remote access VPN does not yet enforce MFA for contractor accounts. On-premises legacy applications cannot integrate with the current IdP and require a separate enforcement mechanism or application modernization.

Root cause: Licensing gaps for legacy app integrations and incomplete contractor onboarding to the new identity platform.
poam_items.resources_required: Azure AD P2 licenses (est. 35 additional seats), 120 hours engineering, contractor identity federation project

poam_items.finding:
Configuration baselines have not been formally documented for all system components within the CUI boundary. Baselines exist for workstations (CIS Benchmark Level 1 applied via Intune) but are absent for three on-premises servers running CUI-adjacent services and two network devices (Cisco switches) that segment the CUI enclave. Without documented baselines, deviations cannot be detected or enforced consistently.

Milestones: (1) Document baselines for on-prem servers by 2026-05-15. (2) Document baselines for network devices by 2026-06-01. (3) Integrate into SIEM alerting by 2026-07-31.
poam_items.resources_required: 80 hours SA time, SIEM integration work (est. 40 hours)

poam_items.finding:
Vulnerability scanning is not performed on a consistent scheduled basis. Tenable Nessus is licensed and deployed but scans are run ad hoc rather than on a defined cadence. The last authenticated scan of the CUI enclave was conducted 47 days ago. Unauthenticated scans of public-facing systems run weekly but do not cover internal CUI assets. No formal remediation SLAs are documented.

Current state: Tenable operational, credentialed scan profiles configured, scheduling not enforced, results not formally reviewed or assigned for remediation.
poam_items.resources_required: 16 hours to configure scheduled scans and review workflow, 8 hours to document remediation SLA policy

poam_items.finding:
Vulnerability remediation is not being performed in accordance with defined risk-based timelines. Critical and high findings from the most recent scan remain unaddressed beyond 30 days. There is no formal remediation tracking process connecting scan findings to tickets or POA&M entries. Two CVEs rated 9.0+ have been identified on internal servers and require patching or compensating controls.

CVE-2024-38063 (Windows TCP/IP RCE) — affected host: SRVDC01. CVE-2024-43491 (Windows Update Servicing Stack) — affected host: SRVAPP02.
poam_items.resources_required: Emergency patching window required. Estimated 8 hours for patching and verification. Change management approval needed.

poam_items.finding:
The organization has not conducted a tabletop or functional test of its incident response capability within the past 12 months. An IR plan exists (v1.2, dated 2025-08-01) but has never been exercised. The plan has not been validated against current system architecture changes including the migration of email to Microsoft 365 GCC High and the addition of the Defender for Endpoint deployment.

The absence of testing means contact lists, escalation paths, and containment procedures have not been validated under simulated conditions.
poam_items.resources_required: External facilitator for tabletop exercise (est. $4,500), 8 hours staff preparation, 4-hour exercise block

poam_items.finding:
CUI at rest is not encrypted on all endpoints within the CUI boundary. BitLocker is deployed and enforced via Intune on 87% of corporate workstations. Eight legacy Windows 10 devices in the engineering lab that process CUI drawings lack BitLocker enforcement due to TPM incompatibility. Three external hard drives used for CAD file backup are unencrypted.

Risk: Loss or theft of any of these devices would result in unencrypted CUI exposure.
poam_items.resources_required: Hardware replacement for 8 lab workstations (budget approval required, est. $14,000) or USB encryption solution for interim compensating control. 24 hours implementation.

poam_items.finding:
The organization does not have a documented cryptographic key management policy or operational procedures for the generation, distribution, storage, access, retirement, and destruction of cryptographic keys used to protect CUI. Keys for TLS certificates are managed informally by the system administrator. No key inventory exists. Certificate expiration monitoring is manual and has resulted in two expired certificates in the past 18 months causing brief service outages.

This is a documentation and procedural gap; no key compromise has been identified.
poam_items.resources_required: 32 hours to draft and approve key management policy, 16 hours to implement certificate lifecycle management tooling (Let's Encrypt automation or Azure Key Vault)

poam_items.finding:
Physical access controls to the server room and engineering lab do not fully meet requirements. The server room uses a combination lock rather than an electronic access control system with individual credential tracking. Visitor log for the engineering lab is maintained on paper and is not reviewed. Badge access to the main facility logs entry but the server room is excluded from the badge system.

Milestones: (1) Install electronic access control on server room (quotes in progress). (2) Migrate visitor log to digital system. (3) Establish quarterly access review.
poam_items.resources_required: Electronic access control installation (est. $8,500 materials and installation), 20 hours project coordination

poam_items.finding:
FIPS 140-2/3 validated cryptographic modules have not been verified across all systems processing CUI. FIPS mode is enabled on Windows endpoints via Group Policy but has not been validated on Linux-based CI/CD pipeline servers or the on-prem file server. Third-party application (SolidWorks PDM) uses its own encryption module of unknown validation status. Vendor has not responded to inquiry regarding FIPS validation.

Requires: System-by-system audit of crypto module usage, vendor confirmation from SolidWorks, and remediation plan for any gaps.
poam_items.resources_required: 40 hours audit work, potential application reconfiguration or compensating controls for non-validated modules

poam_items.finding:
MFA is not enforced for remote maintenance sessions. The IT vendor that performs remote server maintenance connects via a shared admin account over RDP without MFA. This account has local administrator rights on all servers in the CUI boundary. The shared credential is not rotated after each use. This configuration does not meet the requirement to employ multifactor authentication for remote maintenance sessions.

Immediate compensating control applied: Remote access is restricted to business hours only and sessions are logged. Permanent fix requires privileged access workstation (PAW) provisioning for the vendor.
poam_items.resources_required: 16 hours to provision vendor-specific named accounts with MFA, Azure AD guest accounts for vendor, PAM solution evaluation
